summary: Defines the Ghostbusters Record, a signed object holding contact details for the person responsible for an RPKI certificate. Resource certificates themselves hide names, so a contact is needed for problems such as expiry. The data is a severely profiled vCard. Its status is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: The RPKI Ghostbusters Record provides contact details for a maintainer responsible for a resource certificate. It is an optional signed object, and its contact details are not independently verified.

subtitle: A signed RPKI object that carries limited contact details for a certificate maintainer.

tldr.problem: RPKI resource certificates do not provide human-readable contact details. Someone investigating an expired certificate or stale revocation list may need to reach its maintainer.
tldr.mechanism: The Ghostbusters Record is a signed object whose payload follows a limited vCard profile. A certificate authority's maintainer provides the contact data, and an end-entity certificate is used to verify the object.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6493 is Historic. The record is optional, and its contact details are self-asserted rather than independently verified.

facts.label: Required contact method
facts.value: At least one of ADR, TEL or EMAIL

today: RFC 6493 is Historic. It defines an optional signed RPKI contact record whose vCard information is self-asserted.

sections.title: Finding a Certificate Maintainer
sections.content:
RPKI resource certificates use names that are not meaningful to people. When a certificate expires, a revocation list becomes stale, or another problem arises, an operator may need to contact the party responsible for the certificate.

The Ghostbusters Record carries human contact information for the maintainer of a resource-holding certificate authority. The RFC says it is not an identity certificate and does not replace resource registry WHOIS data.
sections.plainLanguage: RPKI certificates do not tell a person whom to contact about a problem. This record carries contact details for the certificate authority's maintainer.

sections.title: The vCard Contact Fields
sections.content:
The record's payload is a limited vCard. It must contain BEGIN:VCARD, VERSION:4.0, a contact name in FN, and END:VCARD. To be useful, it must also include at least one of a postal address, telephone number or email address.

The profile permits organization details and contact methods, but prohibits other vCard properties. The RFC's goal is to include only the information needed to contact the maintainer.
sections.plainLanguage: The required vCard fields identify the card and name a contact. The card must also give at least one way to reach that person or role.

sections.title: Signing and Validating the Record
sections.content:
A Ghostbusters Record is a CMS signed-data object following the RPKI Signed Object Template. An end-entity certificate issued under the relevant CA certificate verifies the object. The object is associated with a CA certificate and published with its subsidiary objects.

Validation applies the signed-object checks, extracts the vCard payload, and checks it against the profile in the RFC. The record is optional; a CA certificate can have zero or more associated records.
sections.plainLanguage: The record is signed and checked as an RPKI object. A validator then checks that its contact card follows the required vCard fields.

sections.title: Contact Data and Trust Limits
sections.content:
The signature verifies the object, but the contact details are self-asserted. The RFC warns that the data have not been verified by the certificate authority that issued the certificate used to validate the record.

Because contact data must be public to be useful, telephone numbers may receive abusive calls and email addresses may receive spam. Operators choose whether to publish a record and which contact details to include.
sections.plainLanguage: The signature does not prove that the contact details are correct. Publishing a phone number or email address can also expose it to unwanted calls or messages.

references.text: Perreault, S., "vCard Format Specification", RFC 6350, August 2011.
Lepinski, M., Chi, A., and S. Kent, "Signed Object Template for the Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI)", RFC 6488, February 2012.
